speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms and if they are progressive?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of appearing "drunk" and feeling clumsy, particularly on the right side, suggest a cerebellar issue. Can you tell me if you have a history of any strokes, head trauma, or other neurological conditions that might explain these new symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a crucial piece of information. Given your history of Crohn's disease and your use of natalizumab for the past year, we need to urgently rule out Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST IMAGES. Do you have any recent history of vision changes, weakness, or speech difficulties?

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: MRI Brain findings show lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images reveal multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement. Additional clinical findings include an ataxic gait, evidence of ataxia on coordination tests, and right upper limb strength of 4/5.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

Given the confirmed MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement and your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, the diagnosis is established. We must immediately discontinue natalizumab and consider initiating immunomodulatory therapy such as IVIG or rituximab to restore immune function.
